frequency_question: How often do major riparian water-sharing treaties successfully get renewed or replaced by a successor accord on or before their expiration date during political transitions in South Asia?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral river water-sharing treaties or major operational extensions between South Asian riparian states facing treaty expiration. Excludes domestic water management acts or non-binding declarations without allocation mechanisms.

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the complete set of major formal river water-sharing treaty negotiations between India and its immediate neighbors in the democratic era.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-basin level state-to-state or provincial arrangements not ratified at the federal sovereign level.
skeleton: Total major bilateral river treaty negotiations attempted in South Asia across the post-Cold War era, categorized by successful formal successor/new treaty signings versus stalled frameworks.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 major comparable bilateral water negotiation attempts = 66 percent baseline historical compliance for formal framework completion.
validity_reason: Regional hydro-diplomacy norms and constitutional structures in South Asia evolve slowly across decades, keeping this structural baseline stable until at least the end of the decade.
